messages:
Maria Chen: Quick question — for the SLO-driven routing work, should circuit-breaker thresholds and fallback chains be stored in tenant config or as global policy with per-tenant overrides? We need low-latency SLOs for enterprise tiers, but they also want predictable fallbacks and quotas.
Ken Patel: leaning toward global sane defaults + tenant overrides. Reason: we can ship stable defaults and keep ops simpler, but allow enterprise to tighten limits. also avoids variant explosion. :+1:
Liam O'Rourke: Agree on defaults, but we should expose the evaluation order in the console. Engineers lose trust if fallbacks happen silently. Need ability to view "why" a fallback took effect for a request.
Anya Sokolov: UX note — console should show per-route SLO, current CB state (closed/half-open/open), last trip time, and recent p95/p99. Also allow temporary manual override for incidents.
Yusuf Ahmed: Telemetry ask: every request should tag policy_id, tier, model_variant, and cb_state. We need an "effective_model" metric so we can count how often small quantized fallbacks are used vs preferred models.
Sam (devex): For docs/SDK we should expose a read-only endpoint to fetch effective routing policy for a customer so customers can simulate behavior locally. Only read-only, no writes. Helps support reproduce issues.
Ken Patel: small policy DSL proposal (very rough):
```
policy {
  id: "policy-enterprise-v1"
  tier: "enterprise"
  targets { p99_latency_ms: 150; availability: 0.999 }
  circuit_breaker { error_rate_threshold: 0.02; min_requests: 100; cooldown_s: 120 }
  fallback_chain: ["redwood-lr-quant", "open-llama-7b"]
  quotas { tokens_per_minute: 500000 }
}
```
Liam O'Rourke: Two internal-api debates: 1) should the router evaluate CB based on aggregated per-region capacity or global? 2) should model-variant fallback be synchronous (router switches path) or async (route original request and also enqueue fallback attempts)?
Maria Chen: On 1) per-region is important because latency SLOs differ by region and crossing regions adds tail latency. On 2) synchronous fallback (try next variant immediately) is simpler and predictable for callers; async reparations would be more complex and surprising.
Anya Sokolov: UX caveat — if we do per-region CBs, console needs a region dropdown and a region-level timeline. Don't clutter main view.
Yusuf Ahmed: Metrics to track for CB tuning: p50/p95/p99 latency, error_rate (5xx+timeouts), healthy_capacity_ratio, queue_length. We'll add a derived signal "cb_risk_score" that combines them for automated suggestions.
Ken Patel: auto-suggestions idea: runway analyzer that recommends increasing cooldown or adding a cheaper fallback when model variant fallback rate > 5% for 24h and p99 > target. Could feed into Optimize later.
Sam (devex): For rollout UX, support staged fallback enablement: e.g., enable fallback for 1% sessions, 10% after 1h, then 100%. Provide canned canary plan in console.
opssim-bot: [simulation-run] policy-enterprise-v1 simulated 10k requests across us-west/us-east/eu-west. Fallback rate: us-west 3.2%, us-east 7.9% (p99 violations), eu-west 0.9%. Suggest tune us-east cb threshold or increase reserved capacity.
Maria Chen: Good catch from sim — highlights per-region tuning. For the internal API, we need a single decision point that accepts: (tenant_id, route, region, observed_metrics) and returns (model_variant, cb_state, reason_code). Keep it small and idempotent.
Liam O'Rourke: Implementation detail: cache decisions for short TTL (e.g., 500ms) to avoid over-evaluating for high qps. But ensure changes in policy propagate quickly when user flips override.
Yusuf Ahmed: Logs example for debugging. Include policy_id and reason:
```
[2026-04-02T15:12:03Z] request=abc123 tenant=tn-42 route=/generate region=us-east policy=policy-enterprise-v1 cb_state=OPEN chosen=redwood-lr-quant reason="p99_exceeded: 220ms > 150ms"
```
Anya Sokolov: Also include a small "why" modal in the console with last 5 decision logs for a tenant-route so support can triage quickly.
Ken Patel: One more security question — do we allow tenants to set fallback chains that reference external models? I think not for enterprise, only from our approved catalog. Prevents exfil risk.
Sam (devex): Agreed. We'll surface allowed-variant list in tenant settings. DevEx can draft help text.
deploy-bot: deploy started: feature/route-policy-operator -> staging (sha: d33f4a)
Maria Chen: OK next steps: Ken + Yusuf + Anya to draft policy schema + telemetry plan. Liam to prototype decision API. Sam will draft console canary UX. I'll sync next Tue. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
